clue.text: Vessel in which second mate's unusually "with it"

indicators.note: something done unusually is done out of the normal order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the 's is read as a plain S, giving the letters of mates to rearrange
with it means fashionable, hip

explanation.surface: On some ship, the second mate is behaving in an oddly trendy way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' rearranges MATES into TEAMS; the 's here supplies a real S rather than being a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship driven by steam power is a kind of vessel.

clue.text: Learner copies the wrong way? A bit of a bloomer

indicators.note: going the wrong way means reading the joined pieces backwards

parts.note: L is the learner driver's plate letter
to ape someone is to copy them, so copies means apes

explanation.surface: A trainee imitates incorrectly and makes a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the wrong way' turns L + APES into SEPAL. A 'bloomer' is a blunder on the surface, but here a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A sepal is one of the leaf-like parts enclosing a flower bud, part of a blossom.

clue.text: Better looking plant?

parts.note: read as a plant that makes the organ of sight shine, one held to improve vision

explanation.surface: Asks whether a plant is more attractive than another.
explanation.walkthrough: The plant was traditionally used to treat eye ailments, so it brightens the eye; 'Better looking' means seeing better, not prettier.
explanation.definitionFit: A small meadow flower once used as a herbal remedy for sore eyes.

clue.text: Corresponding way to sell protective cover on commission

parts.note: mail is armour made of linked rings
a commission is an order for goods or work

explanation.surface: A salesman earns commission selling insurance cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corresponding' means by correspondence, by post.
explanation.definitionFit: Selling goods by post, through letters, is selling by correspondence.

clue.text: Success with principal policies made news

parts.note: a hit is a success
the principal of a school is the head
a party line is a policy

explanation.surface: A party's triumph with its chief policies got into the papers.
explanation.definitionFit: To feature prominently in the newspapers is to make news.

clue.text: No balletic scope, unfortunately, for the flat-footed sort

indicators.note: things gone unfortunately are in a mess, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone flat-footed has no chance of becoming a dancer.
explanation.walkthrough: A flatfoot is slang for a police officer on the beat, not a clumsy dancer.
explanation.definitionFit: Flatfoot is old slang for a uniformed patrolling officer.

clue.text: Comic actor, Polish, with nothing on

parts.note: to polish something is to buff it
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A funny performer from Poland goes about naked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' disguises itself with a capital as the nationality; it is the verb meaning to shine. 'with nothing on' puts O after BUFF in this across answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In opera a buffo is a singer of comic roles, a comic performer.

clue.text: Material support for family firm breaking embargo

indicators.note: one piece breaks into the other, so it sits inside it

parts.note: an embargo is a ban
CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A family business breaks a trade embargo to support its members.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition alludes to 'bringing home the bacon', earning a family's keep.
explanation.definitionFit: The bacon in 'bring home the bacon' is the money that keeps a household.

clue.text: Poet's everlasting incursion?

definitions.meaning: for aye, meaning forever, is a poetic phrase, spelt here with the short form
a raid or sudden attack into enemy ground

explanation.surface: A poet's raid that lasts forever.
explanation.walkthrough: Old poetic 'for aye' means forever; spelt FOR AY and run together it is a word for a raid.
explanation.definitionFit: A foray is a sudden raid into enemy territory, and poets wrote of things lasting forever as lasting for ay.

clue.text: Goes overboard, swallowing sea water initially in dangerous quantities

indicators.note: swallowing means taking in, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: to go overboard is to overdo it

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: Someone falls overboard and swallows dangerous amounts of seawater.
explanation.walkthrough: The held clue dropped 'in' before 'dangerous'; it is a link word. 'initially' takes S from 'sea water'.
explanation.definitionFit: An overdose is an excessive, harmful amount of a drug.

clue.text: Divine pair joined by formal decree

parts.note: an edict is a formal decree issued by an authority

explanation.surface: A heavenly couple are united by an official proclamation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divine' looks like an adjective describing the pair, but it is the verb meaning to foresee.
explanation.definitionFit: To divine is to foretell or guess what will happen, a synonym.

clue.text: Alfalfa from Swiss lake district

definitions.meaning: alfalfa is a fodder plant also known in Britain by another name
a canton and lake in central Switzerland

explanation.surface: A crop is sourced from a region of Swiss lakes.
explanation.definitionFit: The fodder plant is called lucerne in Britain, and Lucerne is also a Swiss lake and the canton around it.

clue.text: Slow Greek ship on lake

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece written on another follows it

parts.note: the Argo was the ship of Jason and the Argonauts in Greek myth

explanation.surface: A slow-moving vessel from Greece sails on a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Largo is the musical direction for a very slow, broad tempo.

clue.text: Pedestrian hired vehicle, extremely exhausted

parts.note: a hackney is a carriage or cab available for hire

indicators.note: extremely asks for the extreme letters of the following word, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone on foot hires a cab because they are completely worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pedestrian' looks like a walker but is the adjective meaning dull; 'extremely' gives ED, the first and last letters of 'exhausted'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedestrian prose is dull and unoriginal, which is what overused, trite writing is.

clue.text: Ancient, after opening of Parliament, is summoned by Speaker

indicators.note: the second piece is placed after the first in the answer
the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: ancient means very old, aged

explanation.surface: An elderly member, at the start of a parliamentary session, is called by the Speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: The Speaker of Parliament fits the surface; here a speaker is anyone calling out names over a loudspeaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Being called by name over a public-address system is how a hotel or airport summons someone.

clue.text: Shul up about overturned water-basin — it's all over the place

indicators.note: one piece goes about another, enclosing it

parts.note: pent means shut up or confined, as in pent-up

indicators.note: overturned in a down answer means the word is flipped upward, read backwards

parts.note: a laver is a large basin for washing, especially in a church or temple

explanation.surface: Be quiet about the upset washbowl, there is water everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The held clue's 'Shul' is a misreading of 'Shut'. A laver is a ritual washing basin; 'overturned' turns it round in this down answer before 'about' puts it inside the word for shut up.
explanation.definitionFit: Something prevalent is widespread, found everywhere.

clue.text: Such great sacrifices trouble Macbeth so

indicators.note: to trouble something is to stir it up, so these letters are disturbed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Grand ritual offerings disturb Macbeth this much.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Greece a hecatomb was a great public sacrifice, originally of a hundred oxen.

clue.text: One coming across Ben, playwright to the monarch

parts.note: Ben Travers was an English writer of farces
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Someone meets a dramatist named Ben who writes for the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' simply joins the pieces; 'coming across' sounds like meeting, but it means crossing over.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who traverses a place crosses it from side to side.

clue.text: Leading model of big store computer

parts.note: leading means chief, main
a frame is a supporting structure, the model on which something is built

explanation.surface: The top model in a department store's computer range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'big store' suggests a large shop, but store is computer memory.
explanation.definitionFit: A large central computer with huge memory, serving many terminals.

clue.text: Join volunteers at home to look after guests

parts.note: to join a club is to enter it
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
in means at home, as in staying in

explanation.surface: Sign up with the reserves while staying home to host visitors.
explanation.definitionFit: To entertain is to receive and look after guests as a host.

clue.text: A girl out of turn

parts.note: miss is a title or word for a girl or young woman

explanation.surface: A young woman speaks when it is not her turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done amiss is wrongly done, out of place or out of turn.

clue.text: George not known in Lancaster?

parts.note: George was RAF slang for the automatic flight controls; a wartime Lancaster bomber had a human flier and no such device

explanation.surface: A man called George is a stranger in the city of Lancaster.
explanation.walkthrough: Lancaster suggests the English city, but it is the Second World War bomber. George was the airmen's nickname for the automatic flying system.
explanation.definitionFit: George is a nickname for the automatic system that steers an aircraft without human control.

clue.text: Head in charge of this subject

parts.note: the top of something is its head

explanation.surface: The boss is responsible for this area of study.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic is the matter under discussion, the theme or field.

clue.text: Factory's twentieth alternative scheme?

parts.note: the plan after a failed first one is the next plan; here the scheme is just plan
T is the twentieth letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A factory's twentieth fallback plan.
explanation.walkthrough: A fallback is Plan B; the twentieth such fallback, counting letters, would be Plan T.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant is an industrial works or factory.

clue.text: Some self-indulgent characters, small and mischievous

indicators.note: some of the letters of the following word are taken as a run

explanation.surface: Certain self-indulgent people are tiny and naughty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' signals a run of letters taken from 'self-indulgent'; 'characters' reinforces that letters are meant.
explanation.definitionFit: An elf is a small mischievous sprite, and elfin describes that quality.

clue.text: Northern Line's new growth points

parts.note: lines can mean verses, and odes are poems in lines

explanation.surface: A new extension point on London's Northern Line.
explanation.walkthrough: The Northern Line is a London Underground line; here it is split into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: In botany, nodes are the points on a stem from which leaves and new shoots grow.

clue.text: Account for former partner, legible

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner
legible writing is plain, easy to read

explanation.surface: Someone must justify an ex-partner whose handwriting is clear.
explanation.definitionFit: To account for something is to give reasons for it, to make it clear.

clue.text: One of the birds top performer in shoot bagged

indicators.note: bagged means put in a bag, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: a bud is a young shoot on a plant
a star is a leading performer

explanation.surface: At a shoot, the best marksman bagged a game bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shoot' and 'bagged' suggest a day of game shooting, but the shoot is a plant's bud.
explanation.definitionFit: The bustard is a large ground-dwelling game bird of open country.

clue.text: Not put into speech? Whip rejected it

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the word is turned backwards

parts.note: the cat-o'-nine-tails is a whip, the cat for short

explanation.surface: A party whip refuses a proposal before it is even voiced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns CAT into TAC. 'Whip' suggests a parliamentary whip, but it is the lash.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacit means understood or implied without being spoken.

clue.text: Characteristic of some cliffs on the Kent coast

definitions.meaning: the quality of being steep and perpendicular
a port town on the Isle of Sheppey in Kent, a county in south-east England

explanation.surface: A feature of certain cliffs found along the Kent shore.
explanation.definitionFit: Steep cliffs have the quality of being vertical, and the same word names a Kentish port.
